title: Bitcoin Barely Moved on the July CPI Print, for the Third Month Running
dek: July inflation landed on August 12 at 3.4% year over year, in line with consensus, with core easing to 2.5%. Bitcoin traded in a band of a few hundred dollars around it, the third consecutive month a major inflation print has failed to move the market meaningfully.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: July CPI came in at 3.4% year over year and 0.1% month over month, matching consensus, with core CPI at 0.2% monthly and 2.5% annually, down from 2.6% in June. Bitcoin moved from about $63,800 to about $64,100 across the four hours around the release, a change of roughly 0.47%, per crypto.news.

body: The July consumer price index, released August 12, came in at 3.4% year over year and 0.1% month over month, matching consensus. Core CPI rose 0.2% on the month and 2.5% on the year, down from 2.6% in June, per The Crypto Times.

The market reaction is the story. Bitcoin moved from roughly $63,800 to roughly $64,100 in the four hours around the release, a change of about 0.47%, on a data point that used to produce swings of 5% to 10%, according to crypto.news. Prices quoted here are as of August 12 and are not the current tape; the desk's boards carry the live figures.
Crypto Briefing reported an initial lift of about 1.3% to near $64,500 that faded back below $64,000 within the session, which is consistent with the same picture: a brief bid, no follow-through.

crypto.news frames it as the third consecutive month in which a major inflation print failed to move bitcoin in either direction, and treats that as evidence the macro trade that dominated 2024 and 2025 has weakened rather than as a signal about what comes next.

Analysts quoted around the print stopped short of drawing a direction from it. Ryan Lee, chief analyst at Bitget Research, said an in-line CPI reading neither forces a hawkish repricing nor delivers a clear dovish catalyst.

This desk reports the print and the reaction and takes no view on what either implies for prices. What is observable is narrow: the number matched expectations, the move was small, and it was small for the third month in a row.
